thread.title: Apple Aside, Six Reasons Why the Tech Sector May Fall

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Apple Aside, Six Reasons Why the Tech Sector May Fall
text:
By Teresa Rivas Aug. 1, 2018 2:14 p.m. ET Tech is the one area that's shining on Wednesday, as tariff worries bog down the rest of the market. But can the party last?
Where we were: Tech's rally has been a major driver of new market highs in recent years, and investors that didn't own FAANG stocks often found themselves lagging. Where we're headed: Tech's long dominance has some worried about when it will end. At least one analyst warns that there's plenty of reason for caution about the sector. Illustration: iStock It's a good day to be a tech investor, with robust third-quarter results from Apple (ticker: AAPL) leading tech higher even as other stocks languish .
It's a welcome change from big disappointments from Facebook (FB) and Netflix (NFLX), but that doesn't mean that worries about cracks in tech's long run have faded. RBC Capital Markets' Lori Calvasina is still wary, reiterating her Underweight rating on large-cap tech today, even with Apple's rise.
She's been bearish on the sector since April. writing that there are a half dozen big reasons that bolster her concern. First, the sector is extremely crowded. That's not surprising, given that funds that haven't chased tech gains have often been shut out of the market rally in recent years. But Calvasina sees " clear signs that sentiment is in the early stages of deterioration," with sell-side Buy ratings on tech stocks at post-bubble highs and starting to slip, and institutional investors looking to get out of FAANG companies–i.e. Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com (AMZN), Netflix, and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL).
Second, Calvasina notes that valuations are back up at post-bubble peaks, on both a price-to-earnings and enterprise-value-to-earnings-before-interest-taxes-depreciation-and-amortization basis. "The sector still looked overvalued as of Monday’s close, particularly on P/E where it was 1.18 standard deviations above average," she writes, a situation that will surely worsen as Apple lifts tech stocks today.
Third, she says that ETF flows may have peaked in the first quarter, arguing second-quarter inflows have "paled in comparison" to those at the start of the year, even after bouncing back from the March rough patch. Fourth, better-than-expected earnings-per-share results and the pace of upward revisions are "starting to decelerate for the sector off peak levels," Calvasina notes.
Her penultimate point is that the stronger U.S. dollar may be a headwind for tech, given its high international exposure. Finally, she says that she's concerned about "the potential for profit taking in tech" following a strong first half of the year, especially for growth funds, which have been very overweight on the sector.
The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) is up 0.7% to $71.40, and has climbed 11.6% year to date.
